body: This used to `continue` for a class that doesn't exist. Now it succeeds.

The check used to load the script. Your new implementations use the cached value instead.
Not sure if this is a desirable change or not.

It is my understanding that `PROPERTY_HINT_RESOURCE_TYPE` (which those types originate from) only supports native classes and global classes in the hint string.

I guess adding a check in case wouldn't hurt though.

As long as it is in the editor the values in `ScriptServer` are updated when changes are made. So it's more like an index then a cache.

In practice the difference comes down to the `is_script_valid` check I guess. Previously we would not offer to create scripts with errors. With the current change we do.

I did not really consider that critical, but if you disagree we can load the script and check it's validity in the editor I guess.
I always advocate for actively rejecting bad state :)
Are there any risks in creating a script with errors? If yes we should probably keep the old behavior.

In theory it should just create a placeholder instance. Placeholder instances are designed with invalid scripts in mind and do store property values speculatively if the prop info from the script is not available.

Only caveat might be `@tool` scripts were at the moment the placeholder would not get converted to a real instance when fixing the script. But https://github.com/godotengine/godot/pull/116368 should take care of that.
It seems to work fine in general. However if the script was never valid the created placeholder is not a `Resource` which fails down the line. Probably better to restrict this to valid scripts.

I did adjust to loading the script in the resource picker, to prevent the edge case mentioned above.

For the icon use case I kept the index check, since the result only controls whether we do some additional requests against `ClassDB`, so there should be no issues even if the script has errors.
